summary: The focus was at a depth of 10 km
text:

title: Ukrainian taxation makes Berlin-Kiev drone talks difficult, newspaper reports
summary: Berlin and Kiev have failed to agree on the export fees so far
text:
BERLIN, November 28. /TASS/. Negotiations on a German·Ukrainian agreement on drone production are progressing slowly due to the customs duties and taxation imposed by Ukraine, Welt am Sonntag quoted internal Defense Ministry documents as saying.
Germany plans to finance the production and purchase from Ukraine more than 2,000 Bars rocket·drones worth approximately €330 million. The Bundeswehr would like to test a version adapted to the needs of the German army, and, if the tests are successful, begin buying the drones starting from 2027. However, Berlin and Kiev have failed to agree on the export fees so far.
The German government called Ukraine’s customs duties and double taxation red lines in the documents.
The newspaper noted that export restrictions also prevented the Bundeswehr from obtaining samples for testing the Flamingo missile, in which it is interested.

title: More than 50 Labour MPs and peers call for new assisted dying legislation
summary: The MPs and peers are calling for new assisted dying legislation within the next decade.
text:
More than 50 Labour MPs and peers call for new assisted dying legislation
- Published
More than 50 Labour MPs and peers have written to Prime Minister Andy Burnham calling for new assisted dying legislation within the next decade.
MPs in September rejected proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing to an end the latest effort to change the law.
But the Labour signatories to a new letter say that fresh legislation should be brought forward within the timescale of the Prime Minister's Ten Year Plan, which will be published next month.
Downing Street told the BBC it was down to parliament rather than the government to decide if the law should change, and Burnham's priority is the improvement of palliative and social care.

text:
UK pensions department confirms cyberattack
November 28, 2026
The UK's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has confirmed that a cyber incident that forced several online services offline was a deliberate attack.
The department said it detected an attempt to gain unauthorized access to its systems late Thursday. Several services, including online portals for state pensions, Universal Credit and Personal Independence Payment (PIP), were taken offline as a precaution. Some remained unavailable as of 5 p.m. local time (1700 GMT) on Saturday.
The DWP said in a statement on X that it was working with the UK's National Cyber Security Centre and Government Cyber Coordination Centre to "bring services back online as soon as possible" while investigating how the attackers had attempted to access its systems.
Officials said there was no evidence that personal information had been compromised.

title: Jury directions on rape myths should always be given, new guidance for England and Wales says
summary: The update to the Crown Court Compendium aims to counter sexual offence myths and stereotypes in court.
text:
Jury directions on rape myths should always be given, new guidance for England and Wales says
- Published
Judges have been told directions to juries on rape myths "should always be given" in updated guidance following Russel Brand's trial.
The Crown Court Compendium, which provides judges with guidance on directing juries in Crown Court trials, was updated on 24 November to add that alerting a jury to the "potential error" of this kind of thinking "remain important and necessary."
This messaging now appears in the official handbook published by the Judicial College, which guides judges and recorders in England and Wales.
It comes after the justice secretary called for new rules to prevent barristers from using rape myths to defend their clients in the wake of the Brand trial.
Brand was sentenced to 10-and-a-half years in prison at the start of November after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

title: Taiwan’s ruling party celebrates its best result in a decade
summary: Taiwan’s ruling party celebrates its best result in a decade Egyptian Gazette
text:
Taiwan’s ruling party secured its best result in a decade in Saturday’s local elections, doubling the number of constituencies it controls, in an outcome expected to anger Beijing.
The Democratic Progressive party (DPP) won 10 of Taiwan’s 22 mayoral and county magistrate races, up from five in its disastrous showing in the last local elections four years ago, The Guardian reported.
The DPP is led by Lai Ching-te, Taiwan’s president, who is detested by Beijing. The Chinese Communist party (CCP) regards Lai as a “separatist” who opposes its plans to unify China and Taiwan. China regards Taiwan, a self-governing island, as part of its territory, a stance that the majority of Taiwanese people reject.
Taiwan’s main opposition party, the Kuomintang (KMT), won 10 races, down from 14 in the last vote. But it retained control of Taiwan’s capital, Taipei, and the neighbouring New Taipei.

Two staff members of Doctors Without Borders, the humanitarian relief agency known by its French initials MSF, were killed in an Israeli strike on one of its clinics in Gaza City on Friday night.
“We are devastated and outraged by the killing of two of our colleagues, both watchmen, in an Israeli strike on one of our Gaza clinics tonight,” MSF said on X on Friday, Al Jazeera reported.
It called the attack a “direct hit” and said the killings bring the number of its staff killed in Gaza to 17.
The agency’s premises were “clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military”, the group said.

title: Writer's 1810 hoax sent hundreds of traders to one London home, blocking street
summary: In 1810, an extraordinary prank unfolded on Berners Street, masterminded by the writer Theodore Hook. He dispatched a multitude of fake letters to local tradesmen, requesting various deliveries to the address of No. 54 Berners Street. The resulting commotion attracted numerous unexpected visitors, creating a delightful chaos. However, as time passed, reactions turned mixed, leading to some criticism.
text:
Authors are perhaps the most notorious of all professions. They spend half their lives surrounded by books and playing with words, yet can sometimes be the most mischievous of them all. And someone in London got a good taste of it two centuries ago.
An account published in 
Jackson's Oxford Journal
 on December 1, 1810, described how an unusual procession of visitors and deliveries brought 
Berners Street
 to a standstill. What began with a few unexpected callers soon turned into a spectacle involving tradesmen, carriages, household goods and even prominent members of London society.
The first knock on the door came early in the morning. A chimney sweep had arrived at a house on Berners Street, London, claiming that he had been summoned to clean its chimneys. The maid who answered the door knew nothing about it and sent him away. But he was not the last visitor. More chimney sweeps soon followed, and before long, carts carrying coal, furniture and other goods began crowding the street.

text:
Lagos is sinking at a median rate of five millimetres annually, increasing the state’s vulnerability to coastal flooding as sea levels rise, a new scientific study has found.
The study, published in the journal Science Advances on Friday, found that land beneath several parts of Lagos is gradually sinking, with the eastern and western outskirts experiencing faster subsidence than the central districts.
The research, titled Sinking Cities: Latent Flood Risk in Africa’s Coastal Megacities, examined land movement in 20 major African coastal cities using satellite radar observations.
It identified Lagos and Alexandria, Egypt, as among the cities experiencing the fastest rates of land subsidence. Alexandria recorded a median sinking rate of six millimetres annually.
The researchers warned that the combination of sinking land and rising sea levels could significantly increase the number of people and properties exposed to coastal flooding in the coming decades.

title: Afghanistan school blast kills 10 students, injures more than 110
summary: Afghanistan school blast kills 10 students, injures more than 110 Egypt Independent
text:
At least 10 people have been killed and more than 110 injured after an explosion near a school in Afghanistan’s northeastern Kunar province, a Taliban spokesperson says.
Preliminary investigations show that the blast happened at a storage depot holding explosives belonging to mining companies.
The deadly incident was the result of negligence and a lack of safety precautions, initial reports found, according to the spokesman.
A number of mining operations are located in Kunar province, which borders Pakistan.
It comes three months after an explosion at an education center in Afghanistan’s capital city of Kabul injured at least 42 children. At least 35 of those admitted to hospital in the aftermath of that attack were aged between 10 and 15, Reuters reported.

summary: Attached to its factory in Wolfsburg, Germany, the huge pillars have space for up to 800 cars, and serve as an attraction in their own right.
text:
Now that's a multi-storey! Inside Volkswagen's amazing glass towers which hold 800 vehicles for new owners to pick up straight off the production line
Volkswagen's glass towers offer shoppers an immersive buying experience like no other.
Attached to its factory in Wolfsburg, Germany, the huge pillars have space for up to 800 cars, and serve as an attraction in their own right.
Stunning photographs this week show the storage facilities filled with vehicles of every colour imaginable, illuminated by strip colour lighting.
Fully automated racks move an average of 500 new cars, which are delivered and then picked up each day.

An explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan kills 10, wounds 110
KABUL, Afghanistan — An explosion at a primary and middle school in the eastern Afghan province of Kunar Saturday killed 10 people and wounded another 110, most of them children, officials said, adding that the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for explosives.
Kunar Culture and Information Director Sami ul Haq Bayan said initial information indicated the blast at the school on the outskirts of the provincial capital, Asadabad, occurred due to negligence at the depot storing explosives belonging to mining companies. text:
My father’s job in mining meant that our family had to move around a lot. My sister and I changed schools quite a few times, from my first to my final year. Most were Christian missionary schools, barring the last one, which belonged to a well-known chain of schools in India.
Besides the differences in local ethos and belief systems, what was common in these schools was that they were located in remote towns across the country: Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh. In our case, they were accentuated by my father holding a senior position in his organisation. Let’s say we were officers’ children, part of the so-called privileged class of the place we lived in.

Yund's qualifying-payment count fell from 116 to 93, leaving him 27 payments short of the 120 required for Public Service Loan Forgiveness, a federal program created in 2007 that cancels the remaining student loan debt of borrowers working for a government or nonprofit employer.

text:
The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea on Saturday rejected, by 18 votes to 3, Argentina's request for provisional measures to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, concluding that it lacked prima facie jurisdiction because Argentina's claims would require determining which state holds sovereignty over the islands, a question outside the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea.

A spate of alcohol poisonings in Iran has led to deaths and serious injuries including blindness.
Two years after four people were executed for distributing contaminated alcoholic beverages – causing the deaths of 17 people and leaving 199 with injuries, including blindness – another spate of mass alcohol poisoning has swept through Iran.

text:
DONETSK, November 28. /TASS/. Emergencies Ministry personnel spent nearly nine hours clearing the rubble of a private house that collapsed in Makeyevka following a strike by the Ukrainian armed forces. The bodies of four people have been recovered, the press service of the Russian Emergencies Ministry’s regional directorate told TASS.
"The rubble-clearing operation lasted around nine hours," the statement said. According to the ministry’s Max channel, the collapsed private house was located in the Chervonogvardeysky District and belonged to two owners.
"While clearing the rubble, Russian Emergencies Ministry personnel recovered the bodies of four victims - a 58-year-old woman, a 45-year-old man, a 23-year-old woman, and a 17-year-old girl," the ministry said. It added that one residential unit had been completely destroyed in the strike, while the roof and ceiling of the other had collapsed, with personal belongings and furniture destroyed by fire across an area of 15 square meters.

text:

I had first heard of it from a Mexican friend who has done adventure travel around the world. “Camino Copalita is the best one, you have to do it!” she told my wife and I. This was no ordinary vacation. To begin with, the website has a decidedly “non-touristy” vibe and very matter-of-factly outlines the basics of the trip. title: South Africans to Spend Record US$18.8bn
summary: A lender's survey projects record December spending of US$18.8 billion in South Africa, but households are cutting travel and barbecues to afford basics. The post South Africans to Spend Record US$18.8bn appeared first on The Rio Times .
text:
South Africans to Spend Record US$18.8bn
A record headline figure hides households that are cutting travel, barbecues and gifts to cover food and fuel.
South Africa: Consumers
South African households plan to spend a record R326 billion, in South African rand (about US$18.8 billion at about R17.37 to the dollar), this December, according to a survey released in late November 2026 by Wonga, a South African short-term lender. The average planned spend is R7,658 per person (about US$441), up 21% on last year.
Yet the same poll finds that nearly half of respondents feel financially worse off than a year ago. They rated the year 3.7 out of 10, the lowest score since 2020, when Covid hit.

title: Chicago crash: 4 injured, 2 critically, in fiery rollover crash on South Trumbull Avenue in Little Village, Chicago police say
summary: Chicago crash: 4 injured, 2 critically, in fiery rollover crash on South Trumbull Avenue in Little Village, Chicago police say ABC7 Chicago See more headlines & perspectives on Google News
text:
CHICAGO (WLS) -- Four people were injured, two critically, in a fiery rollover crash early Saturday on the city's Southwest Side, Chicago police said.
The crash happened around 1:51 a.m. in the 2100 block of South Trumbull Avenue in Little Village.
A vehicle was traveling on Cermak Road when it jumped a curb and struck a pole, police said.
Video from the scene appeared to show a vehicle had rolled over and caught on fire.
A 19-year-old man driving the vehicle was taken to a hospital in critical condition for body trauma, CPD said. A 22-year-old woman who was passenger was also taken to a hospital in critical condition for burns.
Two other passengers, a 19-year-old woman and a 21-year-old man, were also taken to hospitals with minor injuries.
Citations were issues, police said. No further information about the crash was available.
CTA buses were temporarily rerouted in the area due to a street blockage, officials said.

Azerbaijan's opposition leader Ali Karimli: A year behind bars
November 28, 2026
A year after his arrest, Azerbaijani opposition leader Ali Karimli remains in prison.
Karimli has denied charges of attempting to seize power by force, calling them politically motivated. He is the chairman of the Azerbaijani Popular Front Party (APFP), one of the country's main opposition parties.
Karimli is on trial alongside Mammad Ibrahim, his longtime political adviser and a senior party official. Ibrahim has previously served time in prison. text:
Ukraine's international drone alliances with Germany and others
November 28, 2026
Germany and Ukraine want to further boost their defense cooperation. Following a meeting in Berlin with his Ukrainian counterpart, Yevhenii Khmara, German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius announced that drones for Ukraine will be manufactured in Germany in the future.
The project involves the Ukrainian reconnaissance drone known as the "Babka" ("Dragonfly"). Germany is investing around €34 million in the project, according to Pistorius. German company Wingcopter and Ukrainian manufacturer Shadow Flytech have established a joint venture specifically for this purpose.

Sudan Fighting Pushes Families Over Border
Local groups are counting new arrivals in Blue Nile, North Kordofan and South Sudan faster than UN tables can. Key claims about who holds the ground remain unverified.
Conflict: Sudan
Thousands of civilians fled fresh fighting in Sudan’s Blue Nile and Kordofan regions this week, local groups said on Friday 27 November 2026. They are heading for Ed Damazin, the Blue Nile state capital, and El Obeid, capital of North Kordofan, inside Sudan and, across the border, for South Sudan’s Upper Nile state.
The Sudanese army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), a paramilitary group, have fought each other since April 2023. The UN migration agency has counted only part of this wave, in West Kordofan, so local groups are the first to put numbers on Blue Nile and Renk.

summary: South Africa’s Constitutional Court cleared National Health Insurance on Friday 27 November. The President and Health Department now decide when it starts. The post Court Clears South Africa’s Health Law appeared first on The Rio Times .

Court Clears South Africa’s Health Law
The judges settled how the law was made, not whether it will work. The timing, the cost and the remaining court cases are still open.
Health Policy: South Africa
South Africa’s Constitutional Court, its highest court on constitutional questions, cleared a first legal hurdle on Friday 27 November 2026 for National Health Insurance (NHI), a single state fund to buy care. The law is still not in force, and the next step belongs to President Ramaphosa and the Health Department.
The court dismissed challenges brought by the Board of Healthcare Funders (BHF), the industry body of medical schemes and administrators, and by the Western Cape provincial government. Both asked whether Parliament, and in the Western Cape case its provincial chamber, ran a meaningful public participation process before it passed the Act.

title: Pirates seize cargo ship in Gulf of Aden
summary: The crew members took shelter in a secure compartment, and no injuries have been reported
text:
NAIROBI, November 28. /TASS/. Armed pirates have seized a cargo ship in the Gulf of Aden, approximately 220 km northwest of the Somali port city of Bosaso, the Maritime Security Centre Indian Ocean (MSCIO), operating as part of the European Union’s Operation Atalanta naval mission, reported.
According to preliminary information from the center, six armed pirates boarded the vessel. The crew members took shelter in a secure compartment, and no injuries have been reported. The circumstances of the incident are being investigated.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) center also reported the seizure of the cargo ship in the Gulf of Aden. According to the center, the attackers have taken control of the vessel.
The vessel’s name and nationality, as well as the number and nationalities of its crew members, have not yet been disclosed.
Vessels operating in the area have been advised to exercise heightened vigilance and immediately report any suspicious activity.

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea on Saturday rejected Argentina’s request to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falkland Islands (Malvinas), saying the case could not be separated from the dispute over who owns the islands.
The tribunal is based in Hamburg and is an independent judicial body set up under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

title: Dad left his $3million estate to his new wife after promising we'd inherit what was left. Now she's told us we're getting nothing: VANESSA STOYKOV
summary: A father's promise. A $3million estate. And a widow who says his children won't inherit a cent. Vanessa Stoykov explains the mistake that leaves many blended families exposed.
text:
Dad left his $3million estate to his new wife after promising we'd inherit what was left. Now she's told us we're getting nothing: VANESSA STOYKOV
By VANESSA STOYKOV, MONEY EDUCATOR
Published: | Updated:
Dear Vanessa,
My father passed away four months ago at the age of 76, leaving behind an estate worth approximately $3million.
My parents were married for 42 years before my mother died. They worked incredibly hard, paid off the family home and built up a comfortable retirement together.
Mum always told us that everything they had worked for would eventually go to their three children.
Two years after Mum died, Dad met a woman 15 years younger than him. They married quite quickly, but we were happy he had found someone.

text:
Ukraine marks the Day of Remembrance of the Victims of the Holodomor on the fourth Saturday of November each year, which falls on Nov. 28 in 2026.
Ukraine experienced three major famines in the 20th century: in 1921-1923, 1932-1933, and 1946-1947. The 1932-1933 famine was the deadliest and has been recognized by Ukraine and some other countries as a genocide of the Ukrainian people carried out by the government of Soviet dictator Joseph Stalin.
The Holodomor was preceded by the forced collectivization of farms and a campaign known as "dekulakization" — mass repression, property confiscation, and deportations targeting relatively wealthy and independent peasants, known as "kulaks," and their families.

text:
Residents of Jordan Valley vow to remain after Israeli bulldozers raze homes
The latest Israeli attempt to expel the Palestinian residents of Khirbet Samra, located in the northern Jordan Valley of the occupied West Bank, resulted in the demolition of all structures in the community on Sunday.
The demolition spared nothing, not even livestock troughs, residents told Middle East Eye.
The Israeli army went further, burying the debris to ensure the residents could not salvage or reuse any of it.
Currently, the remaining residents of Khirbet Samra are living in tents provided by human rights organisations. Yet, despite everything, they say they are determined to stay.
Dhiab Daraghmeh, a resident, said that more than 15 structures were demolished, including family homes, sheep pens, shelters for young livestock, and storage areas for fodder and hay.

summary: Afghanistan school blast kills 7, injures up to 99 Egyptian Gazette
text:
An explosion near a school in Afghanistan’s ‌northeastern Kunar province killed seven students and injured up to 99 others on Saturday, a spokesperson for the Taliban Interior Ministry said.
Preliminary reports indicated the explosion originated at a depot storing explosives belonging to mining companies near the school, spokesperson Abdul Mateen Qani said in a statement.
Kunar province, which borders Pakistan, is home to a number of mining operations.
The blast occurred in the Andarsir area of Asadabad district, Qani ‌said, adding that authorities were investigating and would release further details once they had completed their inquiry.
In August, an explosion at an education centre in the Afghan capital city Kabul injured at least 42 children, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan.

title: Kimi Antonelli leads Mercedes one-two in Qatar Grand Prix practice
text:
Kimi Antonelli continued his impressive run as newly crowned Formula One world champion by setting the pace in both practice sessions at the Qatar Grand Prix on Friday, leading Mercedes teammate George Russell in a dominant one-two under the Lusail floodlights.
The 20-year-old was fastest in the opening session with a lap of 1:23.217 on medium tyres, 0.507 seconds clear of Russell, who was running on softs.
Antonelli then improved to 1:23.077 in a second practice session that was interrupted by two red flags, with Russell closing to within 0.127 seconds.
The Mercedes pair finished ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri, who were third and fourth respectively, while Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar took fifth and sixth.
Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were seventh and eighth, with Racing Bulls teammates Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad completing the top 10.
The session ended under a virtual safety car after Hamilton stopped on track with a loss of power.

title: Election day rescue of hikers trapped in floodwaters at Lerderderg Gorge
summary: The Victoria Police helicopter crew spotted four of the hikers trapped in the gorge by rising floodwaters after significant rain across the state on election day.
text:
Group of hikers rescued from rising floodwaters in Lerderderg Gorge
Search crews have rescued a group of hikers who got caught in rising floodwaters in Lerderderg Gorge in central Victoria.
The gorge is a popular attraction within the 44,000-hectare Wombat-Lerderderg National Park.
The group set off on the hike after significant rain across the state caused fast-flowing water to rise in the gorge.
Five hikers were rescued earlier in the day before the Victoria Police helicopter was called in to help find another four members of the group who were unable to exit the gorge due to the rising waters.
The hikers had to be guided to safety along a higher ridge line.
The State Emergency Service Bacchus Marsh Unit has urged hikers to avoid the Werribee and Lerderderg Gorge until floodwaters recede.
Victoria Police said no-one was injured.

title: Kidist Tesfaye: The Ethiopian-American whose trip home led to Ethiopia’s first femtech start-up
summary: At 23, Kidist Tesfaye abandoned a promising career in US banking to volunteer at a government hospital in her birth country. Ten years on, the YeneHealth founder talks about her scepticism of imported healthcare solutions, and her disillusionment with corporate America.
text:
By the time Kidist Tesfaye joins me for an interview over Zoom, it is well past her usual morning coffee, a ritual she has grown particularly fond of since returning to Ethiopia a decade ago. At YeneHealth, the company she founded in 2022, there is neither an electric coffee maker nor an espresso machine. Instead, staff roast and grind their own beans before brewing fresh coffee in a traditional clay pot known as a jebena.
Born in Ethiopia but raised in the US from the age of two, Tesfaye soon discovered upon returning home that participating in a traditional coffee ceremony was not entirely a matter of choice.
“Coffee’s a must, whether you like it or not,” she says with amusement. “You either drink it, or you sit there while they’re drinking and you have to participate.”
Learning to slow down over a cup of coffee was part of a wider cultural adjustment for someone accustomed to the fast-paced world of American banking.

The Swiss air quality monitoring organisation placed Lahore at the top of its ranking for global major cities for the 9am to 10am period on Nov 28, with Kabul second at an AQI of 304 and Delhi third at 238.
The ranking at that time showed other cities in the region reporting high pollution levels, with Dubai at an AQI of 168, Kathmandu 166, Kolkata 161 and Karachi 160. Cairo, Chengdu and Kampala also featured among the 10 most polluted major cities.
Lahore’s AQI of 400 fell in the hazardous category, according to IQAir’s scale, which ranks AQI above 300 as such. Exposure to such pollution can pose serious risks, particularly to children, older people and those with respiratory or cardiovascular conditions.

An archaeological mission led by Greek researchers has uncovered evidence suggesting a monumental building in Alexandria could be the royal mausoleum of Egypt’s Ptolemaic dynasty, where its kings and Macedonian ancestors were buried.
The structure, dating to the reign of Ptolemy IV Philopator (245-204 BC), stands in the ancient city’s Royal Quarter. Excavations by the Hellenic Research Institute of Alexandrian Civilization revealed that its foundations form a square, slightly larger than the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
Archaeologist Calliope Limneos-Papakosta said a recently discovered underground tunnel helped researchers identify previously unknown walls and establish the building’s dimensions. Its location, surrounding wall and archaeological dating support the theory that it is the ancient royal tomb, known as the Sema or Soma.

DUBAI, Nov 28 (Reuters) - Iran's flogging of a female singer this week for offending public decency was a display of force by an embattled clerical elite straining to uphold public obedience it once took for granted, Iranian insiders say.
Parastoo Ahmadi, 29, and four members of her production team received 74 lashes each on Monday for a livestreamed performance in a caravanserai near the holy Shi'ite Muslim city of Qom in which she had bare shoulders, no headscarf and male musicians, defying Iran's theocratic legal code.

title: Lagos sinking by 5mm annually, faces rising flood risk – Study
summary: Lagos sinking at about 5mm a year, a new study finds, exposing millions to flood risk by 2050 as Alexandria and Luanda also subside across Africa’s coast. Read More: https://punchng.com/lagos-sinking-by-5mm-annually-faces-rising-flood-risk-study/
text:
Lagos and several other major African coastal cities are sinking at rates that could worsen flooding risks, with some experiencing land subsidence of up to six millimetres annually, a new study has found.
The study, titled Sinking Cities: Latent Flood Risk in Africa’s Coastal Megacities, published on Friday, examined land movement in 20 major coastal cities across the continent using satellite radar data.
The researchers found that Alexandria, Egypt, had the highest median sinking rate of about 6mm per year, followed by Lagos, at 5mm annually.
In simpler terms, Lagos sinks by about half a centimetre or roughly the thickness of three stacked US pennies every year, according to the study.
Luanda, Angola, was also sinking significantly, at approximately 3.8mm per year.
The findings showed that the sinking rates in Alexandria and Lagos were substantially higher than those represented in the 2021 estimates of the United Nations’ Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.

title: Hawaii woman's kindness reunites Chicago family with long-lost photo albums
summary: Rosa Lopez discovered old family photo albums outside her condominium in Waikiki, Hawaii, and decided to help. After researching, she found the albums belonged to a family in Chicago. Anna Richardson and her mother traveled across the country to retrieve their family memories. Upon meeting Lopez, they reflected on the history preserved in the photographs. This encounter highlights the importance of family history and acts of kindness.
text:
One of the saddest things about life is that no matter how much we want to, we cannot relive a moment. Once it is gone, it is gone. The laughter of loved ones, the smiles on their faces and the momentary happiness all pass away and fade into the depths of our memory, until one day, when we find the photo albums in an old cupboard, all the memories come rushing back as if someone has opened a dam of memories, and river-like tears just flow without a break.
Photographs have a peculiar way of keeping time still. text:
Pharmacies get new powers to swap prescriptions during shortages
- Published
Pharmacies are being given more freedom over the prescription medicines they can give to patients when items are out of stock.
Staff will be able to offer the same drug in a different strength or form â two 5mg tablets in the place of a 10mg pill, or a cream instead of an ointment, for example.
The change should help patients avoid repeat trips to their GP for an alternative prescription when the issue can be resolved safely and easily at the chemist.
And for the first time, children in England who miss their flu vaccination at school will be able to receive it at a pharmacy instead.
What can be swapped?
For decades, pharmacists have usually had to provide exactly the medicine prescribed by a doctor under rules set out in the 1968 Medicines Act.

LAHORE: During checking at Raiwind Railway Station, the railway police’ special branch staff recovered on Friday two dogs being transported illegally, without booking, in the Allama Iqbal Express (9-Up) power van.
According to officials, the train’s power plant operator, Mohammad Khan, allegedly charged Rs5,000 for transporting the dogs from Karachi, without booking them under the prescribed railway procedure.
The animals were reportedly to be handed over to a person at Kot Lakhpat Railway Station.
The police initiated legal proceedings against the operator, registering a case against him for violating railway regulations.
The dogs were subsequently booked, and a fine of Rs7,690 was deposited into the railway’s account, officials said.

Heavy rains affect 2,000 families in Peru’s Piura and 47,000 people in Ecuador, where 34 deaths have been reported.
Several cities in Peru and Ecuador are facing major flooding after downpours in the region linked to an exceptionally strong El Nino.
In the city of Piura, capital of the Piura region in northern Peru, waist-high water filled the streets following 12 hours of heavy rains that began on Thursday.
Some 2,000 families have been affected by the rains in Piura, according to preliminary reports, National Institute of Civil Defense chief Luis Vasquez told the RPP radio station.
“This is just the first heavy rain from the El Nino phenomenon and look at how it’s treating us,” said resident Pierre Garavito, as a refrigerator bobbed in the water inside his home in Piura’s Santa Margarita neighbourhood.
“I’ve lost everything … This is how all the residents in the neighbourhood are,” he said.

The crash was caused by a technical error during landing, the Polsat TV channel reported, citing the office’s Spokesman Przemyslaw Nowak.
Polish law enforcement authorities believe the crew of the Tu-154M aircraft had incorrect information about the plane’s altitude during landing. The aircraft’s instruments showed an altitude about 150 meters higher than the actual one, causing the plane to begin descending too late, Nowak said.

summary: Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia's nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack
text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday (November 27, 2026) unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine and said Russia would add five more to the country's fleet by 2030, according to footage released by the Kremlin.
At the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk, Mr. Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm submarine, marking its formal transfer to the navy.
"Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance," he said.
Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia's nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack.
Mr. Putin said the navy would receive five more by 2030, including three vessels from the Yasen-M class, the same class as the Perm.
The submarines can operate in "any part of the world's oceans" while carrying a range of cruise missiles, he added.

An international team of marine geologists using a remotely operated submarine in an abyss in the western Pacific Ocean has found evidence of the deepest-known explosive volcanic eruption on Earth as much as 6,500 meters below the surface.
The researchers sailed to the Mariana Trench, among the deepest oceanic valleys on the planet, to deploy a remotely operated vehicle, or ROV, called Jason/Medea. They used the ROV to study the trench walls around the deepest-known point of seabed on Earth, called the Challenger Deep.

summary: Ecuador reported 34 deaths and 47,000 people affected by heavy rains as at Nov 27.
text:
El Nino-linked deluges flood cities in Peru, Ecuador
PIURA, Peru – Several cities in Peru and Ecuador faced major flooding on Nov 27 after downpours in the region linked to the exceptionally strong El Nino phenomenon.
In Piura, capital of the eponymous region in northern Peru, waist-high water filled city streets following 12 hours of heavy rains that began a day earlier.
Some 2,000 families have been impacted by the rains in Piura, according to preliminary reports, National Institute of Civil Defence chief Luis Vasquez told the RPP radio station.
At the home of Pierre Garavito in Piura’s Santa Margarita neighbourhood, a refrigerator bobbed in the water.
“This is just the first heavy rain from the El Nino phenomenon and look at how it’s treating us. Everything, I’ve lost everything... This is how all the residents in the neighbourhood are,” he said.
Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori postponed a trip to Colombia due to the crisis and said she plans to travel to the affected areas.

text:
In 2004, Rudhramoorthy Cheran published Meendum Kadalukku (Once Again, The Sea), one of his many poetry collections. In its preface, he wrote a seemingly ordinary but deeply unsettling line. Recalling an anthology of contemporary poetry compiled by a friend, whose biographical note stated that Cheran’s collected poems had been published in 2000, Cheran wrote: “I have never been confident that I would ever manage to complete writing all my poems.”
Cheran, one of the brightest voices in contemporary Eelam Tamil poetry, died in Toronto on November 18 at the age of 66. A poet, journalist, playwright and academic, Cheran’s writing spanned more than four decades, during which Sri Lanka witnessed the escalation of ethnic violence, the emergence and defeat of Tamil uprising, and the destruction and displacement of a people.

title: Brent, WTI and the benchmarks that determine how much you pay for petrol
text:
The UAE will announce its December petrol prices on Monday amid hopes they will continue on a downward trend following November's surprise drop.
Brent is on track for a 14 per cent decline this month, while West Texas Intermediate is on pace to retreat about 17 per cent.
UAE petrol prices are not directly tied to Brent. Fuel at the Emirates' pumps has largely been in sync with global oil market movements since 2015, when deregulation was introduced.
Brent and WTI have similar traits, but a number of key dynamics set them apart.
The lowdown
Brent is the global benchmark for oil, pricing up to 80 per cent of internationally traded crude. It comes from North Sea fields, including Brent, Forties, Oseberg, Ekofisk and Troll. Its price is assessed by Platts and futures are listed on the ICE.

MOSCOW, November 28. /TASS/. The Ukrainian armed forces lost over 210 troops, 83 heavy combat multicopters, and 46 drone control posts over the past 24 hours as a result of actions by Russia's Battlegroup West, Leonid Sharov, press center head, said.
"In total, within the area of responsibility of Battlegroup West, combined arms units and unmanned systems forces destroyed over 210 Ukrainian servicemen, 12 vehicles, and one piece of field artillery over the past 24 hours," Sharov said.
According to him, air defense crews and mobile fire teams shot down 32 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles, four loitering munitions, and 83 heavy combat multicopters belonging to the Ukrainian armed forces.
Additionally, 46 drone control posts, a cellular communication tower, 22 robotic systems, and an enemy field ammunition depot were uncovered and destroyed.

text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan removed the marital rape exception from its criminal law two decades ago, but the courts have yet to settle whether a husband can be prosecuted for raping his wife, according to a new report by the South Asian Movement for Accessing Justice (SAMAJ), a coalition of 26 organisations convened by Equality Now.
The report, Challenging the Marital Rape Exception in South Asia, led and authored by lawyer Sahar Bandial, reviewed the law in eight countries.
It noted that the Protection of Women (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2006 redefined rape under Section 375 of the Pakistan Penal Code without reference to marital status, so marital rape can in principle attract the same penalty as any other rape. Yet no reported superior court judgement has confirmed this.
Cases described in the media as marital rape convictions have mostly been brought under Section 377, which covers “unnatural offences”.

The Korea Post, under the Ministry of Science and ICT, said it has confirmed that hackers had accessed mailing records containing customers' personal information and is working to determine the full scope of the breach.
The attackers accessed the mobile Internet Post Office's delivery location change service and viewed the names, addresses and phone numbers of recipients of registered mail being delivered between Nov. 17 and 24.

text:
Your Perfect Dream Girl’s premise instantly interested me when I learned about the themes Sukhnidh Kaur planned on exploring in her book. An influencer since her teenage years, now 27, Kaur looks back on a decade of DMs, selfies, and self-doubt in an indictment of patriarchal technocapitalism. Structured as 25 letters addressed to a faceless man, the book brings together journal entries, love letters from men she encountered growing up, real testimonies, and interviews with industry insiders to trace how young urban women's lives are shaped and warped online.
This distortion happens through filters, follower counts, the cruelty of snark forums, the transactional logic of dating apps, and the threats of deepfakes and AI sexbots. Beneath everything is one core argument: that women have always been the most profitable product of technological revolution.

title: North Korean launderers turn to little-known crypto services to move Binance haul: researchers
summary: U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the largest heist in history after $6.3 billion worth of crypto was stolen on Oct. 29.
text:
Paris – North Korean money launderers are moving closer to cashing out some of the crypto stolen in last month’s record Binance hack, turning to little-known online services that can swap the tokens for others and help hide their tracks, blockchain researchers say.
THORChain, an online exchange urged by the FBI last month not to help the hackers, and a “coinjoin” service which helps mask tokens’ origins, have been used by the launderers to move the stolen crypto further out of reach, according to the researchers.
U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the largest heist in history after $6.3 billion worth of crypto was stolen on Oct. 29. About $2.85 billion of the tokens were frozen by their issuers, but the rest remains in circulation. North Korea denies involvement in the hack.

summary: A Ukrainian military intelligence official and a Middle East security official confirmed that the flotilla had turned from heading to Libya.
text:
Paris/London – A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya has turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank a Russian naval corvette in Benghazi port on Nov. 22, three people from military and security services said Friday.
The convoy’s diversion, which has not been previously reported, shows how Russia is acting to protect its naval assets following a Ukrainian sea drone attack that sank a Russian warship in Libya some 2,000 kilometers from the battlefield in Ukraine.
The convoy, which was escorted by a Russian navy frigate, Golovko, turned around near the Strait of Sicily on the same day as the attack in Benghazi, a European military official, who had been tracking the convoy, said.

text:
Washington – Hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter said, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. Reporters could not establish the identity of the hackers, the full scope of the intrusion or whether any data had been stolen.

Son of Hamas chief survives Israeli strike, militant group says
A Palestinian man inspects a vehicle damaged by shrapnel from a projectile following an Israeli airstrike that targeted a residential apartment where the family of Izzeldeen al-Hayya, son of Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya, was staying, according to a senior Hamas official, in Gaza City, in the Gaza Strip, on Friday.
| REUTERS
Cairo – The son of Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya survived an assassination attempt by the Israeli military on Friday, senior Hamas official Basem Naim said.
He said that Izzeldeen al-Hayya and his family had survived a dawn airstrike and Hamas sources said several people, including al-Hayya’s daughter-in-law, had been wounded but there had been no deaths.
The Israeli military had no immediate comment.

title: Taiwan goes to polls in tight local elections as China watches
summary: For the opposition Kuomintang, which advocates friendlier ties with China, the results could reorder the field for the 2028 presidential election.
text:
Taiwan headed to the polls Saturday for local elections that could reshape the political field ahead of the 2028 presidential contest, with voters galvanized by an unexpectedly close race in the capital Taipei.
Some 19.6 million people are eligible to vote for mayors and county chiefs across 22 cities and counties, with more than 11,000 smaller roles up for grabs. Polls run from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with initial results expected in the evening.
The vote will test whether President Lai Ching-te’s Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) can translate its record run of three straight presidential victories into gains at the local level, where the opposition Kuomintang (KMT) has long been stronger. For the KMT, which advocates friendlier ties with China, the results could reorder the field of politicians vying to challenge Lai in 2028 — a contest Beijing is closely watching.

title: Doomed driver heard desperately trying to escape his sinking car after it crashed into pond, moments before he drowned
summary: A driver drowned on Thanksgiving night after his speeding SUV flew off a Texas road and plunged into a pond.
text:
Doomed driver heard desperately trying to escape his sinking car after it crashed into pond, moments before he drowned
A driver could be heard desperately trying to smash his way out of his sinking SUV after it flew off a road in Texas and plunged into a pond on Thanksgiving night.
The man's frantic attempts to escape were heard by a nearby resident who rushed into the freezing water but was unable to reach him despite two desperate rescue attempts.
The driver drowned inside the vehicle in south Harris County, near Houston, while the man who tried to save him was left haunted by how agonizingly close he had come to reaching him.
Eugene Mayer was at home at around 7pm on Thursday when he heard the sound of the crash near Beltway 8 and Almeda Road.
Realizing a vehicle had careered into the pond, Mayer sprinted from his home and threw himself into the water in a desperate bid to save whoever was trapped inside.
But the combination of exhaustion and the bitterly cold water overwhelmed him.

title: What happens to unused embryos after IVF?
summary: Imagine that after years of struggling to have a child, you finally achieve your dream through in vitro fertilisation. Your joy is overwhelming, but there is something you may not immediately think about. Read More: https://punchng.com/what-happens-to-unused-embryos-after-ivf/
text:
Imagine that after years of struggling to have a child, you finally achieve your dream through in vitro fertilisation. Your joy is overwhelming, but there is something you may not immediately think about. Several embryos created during your IVF treatment may still be frozen in a laboratory, waiting for a decision about their future.
Perhaps you intend to return for another child, or perhaps you have already had the number of children you want; you may even have changed your mind about having another pregnancy. Whatever your circumstances, those embryos remain in storage, and someone must eventually decide what happens to them.

title: Removing British-era place names is ridiculous – English ensures Indian unity
summary: The India Fix: A newsletter on Indian politics from Scroll.
text:
Welcome to The India Fix by Shoaib Daniyal, a newsletter on Indian politics. As always, if you’ve been sent this newsletter and like it, to get it in your inbox every week, sign up here (click on “follow”).
Have feedback, interesting links or think I am wrong? Write to me: theindiafix@scroll.in
India’s Constituent Assembly did not have many bitter fights, overwhelmingly dominated as it was by one party, the Congress. Even a proposal, by none other than the head of the drafting committee, BR Ambedkar, to retain a weak form of separate electorate for Dalits, was struck down with almost no debate.
However, one proposal did see the members of the Assembly clash – and clash hard: that Hindi replace English as India’s official language. For three days the Constituent Assembly debated the idea, in the end accepting a compromise. Both Hindi and English would be official languages, though the latter had a sunset period of 15 years.
However, at the end of the sunset period, nothing much changed.

text:
Republican urgently stops his campaign in runoff election after two young volunteers die in horror car crash
A Georgia Republican who was set to face a runoff election on Tuesday has paused his campaign after two of his young volunteers died in a car accident.
Berti Nagy and Blake Henley, two workers for State Representative Mike Cheokas's reelection campaign, were driving late Wednesday during a storm when their car hydroplaned and hit another vehicle.
Cheokas, who has been in the Georgia House of Representatives for two terms since 2005, announced he would suspend his campaign as a result of the news, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.
'Words cannot express the grief within our team in the wake of such a tragic event,' Cheokas said Thursday.
'However, it pales in comparison to what the families of Berti and Blake are feeling today. Our hearts go out to them, both now and going forward.'

title: Stock loans fall to 13-month low amid wild volatility
summary: SEOUL, Nov. 28 (Yonhap) -- Stock loans in South Korea fell to a 13-month low thi...
text:
Stock loans fall to 13-month low amid wild volatility
SEOUL, Nov. 28 (Yonhap) -- Stock loans in South Korea fell to a 13-month low this week amid increased volatility in stock markets, industry data showed Saturday.
The amount of outstanding margin loans came to 25.04 trillion won (US$18.7 billion) on Friday, marking the lowest level since Oct. 28 last year, according to the data compiled by the Korea Financial Investment Association.
The tally came as volatility heightened in local stock markets this week.
After hitting a record peak in June, the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index has slumped, mainly due to investment fears over artificial intelligence.
 This week alone, trading curbs on the stock markets were activated four times due to wild swings.
(END)

رد أحمد سليمان، عضو مجلس إدارة نادي الزمالك، بشأن مزاعم تقدم لاعبي الفريق الأول بشكوى إلى الاتحاد المصري لكرة القدم، بسبب تأخر المستحقات، بعد أيام من نشرهم بيانًا مشتركًا بشأن هذا الأمر.
وقال أحمد سليمان في تصريحات عبر قناة "إم بي سي مصر 1": "رأيك في بيان لاعبي الزمالك الأخير؟ لما جينا مجلس الإدارة السنة اللي قبلها اللاعيبة مكانتش واخدة فلوسها، وجبنا مدرب وقدرنا ناخد السوبر ونعمل حاجة".
وأضاف: "حصل مشكلة الأرض وفي دروب في العقود، هاتلي مرة لاعيبة الزمالك مأخدتش فلوسها، وهتتحل الإدارة بتسعى، البيان ده حاجة جديدة".
وأكمل: "لولا إن عندنا ماتش في إفريقيا كنت قولت حاجات تانية. اللاعيبة دلوقتي عايزة توصل رسالة".
وتابع: "مفيش حاجة نهائية تتعلق بإن هيكون في شكوى جماعية من لاعيبة الزمالك ولا في 40 سنة جايين لاعيبة الزمالك تقدم شكاوي ضد النادي. كل التزام على نادي الزمالك لأي لاعب أجنبي أو مصري هياخده بكرة أو بعده".

The Indian 'Tamasha queen' whose fans paid for a show that never happened
- Published
Few things could keep Vithabai Narayangaonkar, one of the greatest stars of Maharashtra's folk theatre, away from the stage.
Not even, it would seem, the birth of her child.
In the 1960s, the singer, dancer and troupe leader was performing in Shikhar Shingnapur, a village in the western Indian state, when she went into labour.
"She quietly stepped behind the stage into a makeshift tent while the rest of us continued performing," her daughter, veteran folk artist Mangala Bansode, told BBC Marathi.
Outside, the restless audience kept shouting: "Where is Vitha?"
When Vithabai returned to the stage, she was cradling her newborn son, the seventh of her eight children.
"The audience was stunned, but they quietly left, saying, 'We will watch your performance later'," Bansode recalled.

title: Starshield restrictions cause heavy Ukrainian drone losses, canceled operations — report
summary: In a conversation with The Kyiv Independent, a senior Ukrainian military official called the move a "political decision"
text:
MOSCOW, November 28. /TASS/. Restrictions on the Starshield satellite communication system used by the Ukrainian armed forces have led to heavy drone losses and the cancellation of a number of operations, The Kyiv Independent reported, citing high-ranking Ukrainian military officials.
Specifically, one Ukrainian military source told the publication that the restrictions significantly affected FP-2 medium-range strike drones. According to the source, limitations on Starshield’s operation resulted in "extremely high drone losses" during certain operations, while others had to be called off entirely.
Another senior Ukrainian military official called the move to restrict the Starshield system a "political decision."
Earlier, Vladimir Zelensky said the Ukrainian armed forces had also faced difficulties intercepting drones due to ongoing issues with access to Starshield. In mid-November, Zelensky claimed that the Ukrainian armed forces’ access to Starshield had been restricted for five days.

title: Police investigating death of 47yo man in remote NT town
summary: Police are investigating the death of a 47-year-old man south-east of Darwin after an alleged altercation with another man.
text:
Police are investigating the death of a 47-year-old man following an alleged altercation in the Katherine region last night.
NT Police said in a statement that a man was "struck in the head" during an incident involving another man at a property near Pine Creek, about three hours' drive south-east of Darwin, yesterday afternoon.
Police said the injured man was taken to Pine Creek Clinic by family members.
At about 5pm clinic staff reported the alleged assault to police.
The man became unresponsive at the clinic and CPR was commenced.
He was declared dead at about 6pm last night.
An NT police spokesperson said police were investigating whether the incident was "domestic violence related".
"Police have established a crime scene at the clinic and are working to locate the alleged offender," they said.
They said investigations into the incident were ongoing and urged anyone with information about the alleged assault to come forward and contact them on 131 444.

The peso fell to its worst level since April 2015 on Thursday, closing at 19.72 to the U.S. dollar, while depreciating 7.01% during the seven-day losing streak. It has fallen nearly 14% over the past three months and was down 9.54% on the year.
The peso initially climbed 0.64% to 19.57 shortly after opening, but had weakened to 19.657 by 5 p.m.
Banco Base expects the peso to end its losing streak and trade between 19.49 and 19.69 per dollar in a session of reduced liquidity, due to the partial reopening of U.S. capital and bond markets after the Thanksgiving holiday.
Mexico’s currency had not experienced such a prolonged negative stretch since the period from Aug. 31-Sept. 8, 2023, although the depreciation then was less severe (5.07%).

As the scale and reach of variable renewable energies expand around the world, more and more clean energy is being produced. However, more and more of that clean energy is also going to waste. The drone used in the attack on Kuwait that killed two Italians was manufactured in Iran, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Friday.
In an interview with the Italian press, Tajani said: "According to the investigations carried out by the Kuwaitis, the drone was manufactured in Iran."
The attack on Thursday also injured two other people.
It drew condemnation from many countries, and some, including Syria and Saudi Arabia, blamed Iran for it.
Meanwhile, Iran has denied launching the drone, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi calling the incident "suspicious".
"The Iranians say it was not launched from Iranian territory, but, as you know, Iran's proxies, all of Iran's allies, have Iranian-made drones," Tajani told press.

Just like that, the migrant crisis is over – or so said Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. She was responding to figures showing annual net migration has fallen to 77,000, its lowest level this century outside the pandemic.
‘The Government has restored control,’ she declared. But has it, or is this just hubristic fantasy?
It’s true the number of people coming into the country has fallen dramatically from its 2023 peak. Tougher visa controls brought in by Rishi Sunak and carried on by Ms Mahmood have been largely responsible for this welcome drop.

text:
Working poverty in Mexico fell to its lowest level since the indicator was first measured in 2005, thanks to wage recovery and steady economic growth.
Working poverty — defined as someone whose labor income is too low to buy a basic food basket, as determined by national statistics agency INEGI — decreased to 30.5% in the third quarter, a decline of 1.4 percentage points from the second quarter.
The 30.5% figure bettered the previous record low figure, which came in the first quarter of 2026, when it stood at 30.7%.
In year-on-year comparison, labor poverty — as it is also known — decreased by 3.9 percentage points, its largest drop since the third quarter of 2021, when it fell by 5.3 percentage points as the Mexican economy recovered from the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: A former loom house offers a quiet look into Kyoto’s bygone Silk Road
summary: In its heyday, Yosano in northern Kyoto Prefecture used to be filled with the sounds of clacking looms.
text:
Yosano, Kyoto Pref. – For several centuries, daily life on the Tango Peninsula in northern Kyoto Prefecture had a single, inescapable noise as its soundtrack: the clatter of looms weaving silk thread.
Since the early 18th century, the region about two hours north of Japan’s ancient capital has been home to an industry central to the production of silk crepe, the primary material of kimono. In the postwar boom, the sound of the looms was the sound of money itself: Locals called it “gachaman,” a portmanteau of “gachan” (an onomatopoeia for the loom’s sound), and “man” (the Japanese term for ¥10,000), because each mechanical beat was said to earn another stack of cash. At its peak in 1973, the region produced enough fabric to make roughly 9 million kimono a year.
The epicenter of this industry was a bustling street in the town of Yosano so central to the industry it earned the name “Chirimen Kaido” — literally, Silk Crepe Road.

Competitive handbag throwing and high-heel skipping were once acts of political defiance in Perth.
Both disciplines featured in what was originally known as the city's 'Gay Olympics', which ran annually from 1979 to 1999 to raise money for gay and lesbian charities.
They event also pushed for law reform at a time when consensual homosexual sex between men was still illegal in Western Australia; the decriminalisation of which only began in 1990.
Volunteers at the West Pride Archives have been sifting the event's history ahead of Perth hosting the 2030 International Gay Games.
Jo Darbyshire, co-convenor of West Pride Archives said Perth's original games had a strong political edge.
"Being visible out in the community and not being shamed was a huge element to (them)," she said.

title: Aboriginal community captured in 'timeless, beautiful' tintype portraits
summary: When Joan Lamont looks at the greyscale portraits of her Kaurna mob placed side by side, she sees the eyes of her ancestors looking back at her.
text:
Kaurna artists reframe community through tintype photography
When Joan Lamont looks at the greyscale portraits of her Kaurna mob placed side by side, she sees the eyes of her ancestors looking back at her.
"How they look … is like looking back and seeing the old people come back to them," the Kaurna Narungga elder said.
The tintype portraits of her living community members have just finished developing and are drying out on a table next to a makeshift darkroom in a bathroom.
The 83-year-old has just sat for her own tintype portrait taken by Kaurna artists James Tylor and Damien Shen in the Art Gallery of South Australia's courtyard.
Tylor and Shen spent a week in October with a vintage Linhof camera capturing their community in the analogue format.

title: Walker wins Australia's first medal of World Cup season
summary: Bree Walker has won bronze in the opening women's monobob event in Germany, securing Australia's first World Cup medal of the 2026-27 season.
text:
Bree Walker has won bronze in the opening women's monobob event in Germany, securing Australia's first World Cup medal of the 2026-27 season.
In her first race since off-season knee surgery limited her preparation, the two-time Olympian delivered an impressive performance in Altenberg on Friday.
Walker posted the third-fastest time in heat one at 1:00.29, then went even faster in heat two with 59.87 seconds to secure third place overall with a combined time of 2:00.16.
The 34-year-old Queenslander's performance placed her just 0.54 seconds behind event winner Laura Nolte of Germany (1:59.62), and within striking distance of second-placed Lisa Buckwitz, also of Germany (1:59.87).
The medal marks Walker's 18th World Cup podium and her third at the Altenberg track.
"I wasn't too sure after this off-season with my knee rehab what shape I was going to be in, so [I'm] very happy to start the season off with a third place in Altenberg," Walker wrote on social media.

The US military says it disabled the Palau-flagged ship’s propulsion but its crew was unharmed.
The US military says it has fired on a merchant vessel in the Gulf of Oman and claims it was trying to breach an American blockade on Iranian ports.
Military aircraft fired “precision munitions” at the stern of the Palau-flagged M/V Pacific Archer on Thursday, and the “ship’s propulsion was ultimately disabled and the civilian crew was unharmed”, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement.
US officials say the Pacific Archer left the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas before it attempted to run the blockade. Ship tracking websites list the vessel’s destination as Singapore. It is at least the 15th vessel the US military has publicly acknowledged disabling since the blockade began in April, and the sixth since it resumed it in July. The previous vessel was disabled on November 7.

title: Archaeologists in a West Texas rock shelter found a hunting kit left untouched for about 6,500 years
summary: In a remarkable archaeological find in West Texas, researchers uncovered a hunting kit that dates back approximately 6,000 years. The collection features various stone and wooden foreshafts, along with essential hunting tools, including a partial atlatl, which is an ancient spear-throwing apparatus. The diversity of materials suggests varying time periods, unlocking valuable insights into the lifestyles and surroundings of these ancient communities.
text:
A bunch of friends collect their small but most precious belongings in a box or tin, seal it tight, and bury it in a park or garden. The concept of time capsules is fascinating because they are symbolic of the material culture of the time when they were stashed, and they tell you about the habits of people in that age. However, not all time capsules are planned. Some are left behind in a hurry, in a disaster, or simply lost. One such lost artefact was found buried in a West Texas rock shelter, and it is an ancient hunting kit.

summary: The U.S. military has delivered Thanksgiving dinner to troops from Civil War Union troops to Vietnam's War Zone D, a tradition born in wartime.
text:
In November 1966, 12 American soldiers stationed at an isolated outpost in a Vietnamese war zone were about as far from a traditional Thanksgiving at home as they could get.
Their only means of resupply was by air. But the U.S. military was determined to get them Thanksgiving dinner anyway.
A mess sergeant at Bien Hoa prepared turkey and all the trimmings, packed the meal into insulated containers and sent it by helicopter into War Zone D, where three officers and nine enlisted men of a 5th Special Forces detachment sat down to Thanksgiving dinner, according to Defense Department records preserved by the National Archives.
The delivery was one piece of a massive logistical effort the U.S. military has undertaken during wars spanning generations to get traditional Thanksgiving meals to troops serving in combat zones.

People in fire-affected areas are urged to stay up to date with the latest advice via the TasALERT website.

title: F1 driver runs over mechanic's foot in Qatar
summary: Red Bull has copped a fine after French driver Isack Hadjar accidentally ran over the foot of a mechanic who was still working on his car.
text:
Red Bull has copped a fine after French driver Isack Hadjar accidentally ran over the foot of a mechanic who was still working on his car.
Hadjar pulled into the pits during Friday's practice for this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, the penultimate race of the season, but left before all mechanics had finished working on his car.
A mechanic had placed a cooling blower at the left rear tyre, which was not supposed to happen according to the team, as documented in the stewards' report.
Believing he was clear to leave the pit lane, Hadjar began to drive off before the blower had been removed from his car. 
Hadjar ran over a mechanic's foot before driving off. 
"Everyone OK," Hadjar asked immediately after realising he had made contact with a mechanic. 
The mechanic was reportedly unharmed, and Red Bull was fined 30,000 euros ($49,350), with 20,000 euros suspended.

summary: In a groundbreaking study, researchers in Chad have uncovered puncture marks on baboon skulls, suggesting that eagles may prey on these large primates. Out of five examined skulls, three displayed signs typical of eagle talon strikes. This startling discovery raises questions about baboons' vulnerability to aerial predators and encourages a reassessment of early hominin interactions with such threats, potentially reshaping our understanding of primate evolution.
text:
Eagles, with their sharp talons, can be incredibly feisty avians, ones that we perhaps imagine as predators of fairly small animals, such as rabbits or rodents. But we might not imagine an animal weighing more than 20 kilograms being attacked by their sharp claws. However, a discovery in the rocky landscapes of Chad has nudged researchers to reconsider just how vulnerable some of our primate relatives might have been to these predators in the sky.
According to a study published in the 
American Journal of Biological Anthropology
 on November 18, 2026, researchers examining baboon remains from the Ennedi region of northeastern Chad discovered puncture marks on two adult baboon skulls, suggestive of damage caused by eagle talons. Further fieldwork in June 2026 revealed a third skull bearing similar marks.

text:
The Independent National Electoral Commission has urged political parties and other stakeholders in Edo State to mobilise residents for Saturday’s mock accreditation exercise ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The state’s Resident Electoral Commissioner, Obo Effanga, made the appeal at a stakeholders’ meeting in Benin on Friday, saying public participation would help the commission assess its election preparations.
Effanga said the exercise would take place from 8.30 am to 2.30 pm in two polling units in each of the state’s 192 registration areas.

Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office
It comes a month after opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela.
Venezuela will repeal a law that prohibits opposition figures from office, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez has announced.
The legislation, approved in 2024 and criticised for enabling political persecution, targeted those who promoted or supported sanctions against the country.

The law was passed just after fraught elections which the then-incumbent Nicolas Maduro ultimately won amid widespread allegations of fraud.

title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
summary: Quebec's government passed Bill 21 to ban religious symbols for public servants, arguing it was necessary to protect its secularist society. Critics argue the bill weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.
text:
Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill
November 27, 2026
Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld Quebec's ban on religious symbols for public servants.
However, it ruled that provincial lawmakers should be allowed to wear religious symbols in the legislature, Quebec's National Assembly.
Quebec's government passed the bill, known as Bill 21, in 2019, arguing it was necessary to protect its secular society.
Under the law, anyone receiving public services like teachers and police officers has the right to do so without being exposed to overt religious symbols, including hijabs, turbans and yarmulkes.
What did the Supreme Court say about the law?
Chief Justice Richard Wagner said that the law "is rooted in Quebec's legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the (secularism) of the state in a free and democratic society."

text:
Seal Rocks clings to its charm while bracing for another summer influx
For generations of families and surfers, a visit to Seal Rocks has included a stop at its much-loved general store, an enduring landmark in the remote coastal village.
The shop is on the only road into the town on the NSW Mid North Coast, perched at the top of a hill overlooking a crescent-shaped beach, fringed by bushland.
Owned by the Horgan family for more than 70 years, it is reminiscent of a different era captured in the faded photos that cover the walls.
An old telephone exchange box remains inside, while outside there's a working public phone booth — a necessity rather than a novelty in a town where mobile reception remains notoriously unreliable.
Kylie Galea helps run the store and post office.
"There's lots of nostalgia," she said.
"Just about every day there's someone who comes in that says, 'I used to come here when I was a kid, I remember this store'.

title: Christian social worker was discriminated by firm who did not offer him a job because he said 'homosexuality is a sin', Appeal Court rules
summary: Christian social worker Felix Ngole, who was discriminated against after a firm did not offer him a job because of his views on homosexuality, said his case marked an 'important victory' for Christians.
text:
Christian social worker was discriminated by firm who did not offer him a job because he said 'homosexuality is a sin', Appeal Court rules
A charity discriminated against a devout Christian social worker by withdrawing a job offer because of his views on homosexuality, the Court of Appeal ruled.
Felix Ngole thought he was about to join the mental health charity Touchstone Leeds in Yorkshire in 2022, but found himself jobless because of his religious views.
Bosses told Mr Ngole his belief that 'homosexuality is a sin' was incompatible with their values after they discovered a previous dispute he was involved with.
That case related to Mr Ngole's successful legal challenge against the University of Sheffield over its decision to expel him from his MA course in social work for comments he made on social media in 2015 about homosexuality.
Touchstone told Mr Ngole his views went against its own, but offered to reconsider if he could give assurances his beliefs would not compromise his role.

The court determined Tamm did not adequately demonstrate an easement and failed to provide sufficient evidence of the required deed. His appeal based on historical usage was also declined, ultimately reaffirming his neighbors' rights over the contested access paths.
text:
A North Dakota landowner who claimed that a 1993 subdivision map gave him the right to use access roads across his neighbours' properties lost his legal battle after the state 
Supreme Court
 found that he had failed to establish an easement. The dispute centred on two documents recorded at noon on the same day: a property map showing access easements and a deed transferring the middle parcel to a new owner. However, the court found that the landowner could not prove the deed had been delivered before the map was recorded.
In its November 25, 2026 
decision
 in Tamm v. Gatzke, available on Justia, the North Dakota Supreme Court also rejected claims that the access rights arose through long-term use or necessity. It affirmed the lower court's judgment denying Rudra Tamm's request to establish access across his neighbours' land.

Is Iraq facing renewed instability?
Roughly 20 percent of Iraq’s oil reserves are in the semi-autonomous Kurdish region.
The local government runs the oil fields and revenue helps it govern. But now that is in danger.
The federal government has announced control over refineries. Baghdad says it’s losing millions of dollars every month to crude oil smugglers.

Both domestic wine sales and export volumes also fell.

Experts say the global wine industry will need to continue shrinking to address an ongoing oversupply of billions of litres.
Latest figures reveal the shrinking Australian wine industry is now selling more wine than it is producing.
However, a glut of millions of litres remains a critical concern as people continue to drink less wine globally.
Wine Australia's latest Production, Sales and Inventory report shows national wine production in 2025–26 fell 18 per cent to 925 million litres, while just over 1 billion litres of wine was sold.

text:
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday unveiled a new nuclear-powered submarine and said Russia would add five more to the country’s fleet by 2030, according to footage released by the Kremlin.
At the Sevmash shipyard in the northwestern city of Severodvinsk, Putin attended a flag-raising ceremony aboard the Perm submarine, marking its formal transfer to the navy.
“Russia is one of the few countries in the world capable of building powerful nuclear submarines of this kind, weapons with global reach and significance,” he said.
Nuclear-powered submarines are a key part of Russia’s nuclear deterrent because their ability to operate covertly underwater ensures a retaliatory strike capability in the event of an attack.
Putin said the navy would receive five more by 2030, including three vessels from the Yasen-M class, the same class as the Perm.
The submarines can operate in “any part of the world’s oceans” while carrying a range of cruise missiles, he added.

Inquest into baby deaths hears homebirths have doubled since COVID
In the midst of two weeks of heartbreaking testimony about what can go wrong when babies are born outside hospitals, a stark piece of evidence emerged.
A coronial inquest heard the number of babies delivered by homebirth has doubled in Australia since the COVID-19 pandemic.
Deputy Coroner Joan Baptie is investigating the deaths of three babies born by freebirth in northern New South Wales, and a fourth by homebirth in the Hunter Valley.
A homebirth is when a woman plans to have her baby at home under the care of a registered midwife who works in the private sector or is employed by a hospital.
In NSW, up to 600 babies are now born at a midwife-assisted homebirth each year, up from about 280 in 2019.

title: New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking
summary: Cities including Lagos and Alexandria are sinking faster than previously thought, a new study shows.
text:
New satellite data shows how fast some African cities are sinking
- Published
Some of Africa's largest cities are sinking faster than previously thought, new research shows.
Scientists used radar imagery from the European Space Agency's Sentinel-1 satellites to map how much the land beneath 20 African coastal cities had moved.
The study found that some cities - including Lagos in Nigeria and Alexandria in Egypt - were sinking much faster than previously estimated in 2021 by the UN's climate body, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).
While some causes of this sinking, or subsidence, are natural, many are the result of human activities, such as the extraction of groundwater from underneath the Earth's surface.
Lead author Oluwaseyi Dasho said the effects of subsidence "are often invisible in everyday life, but over decades they can substantially increase flood exposure".

Lot feeding has grown exponentially in Australia, with the sector now valued at $4.5 billion.

The longtime husband of Sen. Deb Fischer, R-Neb., died by suicide, her office announced on Friday, after initially saying that he “passed away peacefully” nearly a week ago.
Fischer first released a statement on X on Sunday announcing that her husband of more than 50 years, Bruce Fischer, died the day prior to the post “doing what he loved the most, spending time outdoors.”
Fischer, a Republican who has served in the Senate since 2012, wrote in the first statement that she would “cherish the decades we spent building a family in the Nebraska Sandhills.”

On Friday morning, a spokesperson for the senator released a statement on a “sad update in the death” of Bruce Fischer.
“Initially, it was believed that Bruce passed peacefully at home,” the statement on X read. “Upon further investigation, it was learned that Bruce chose to end his life.”
