title: Don't worry about AI... Quantum computing might well get you first, Bank Of England boss warns
summary: Even as the threat of cyber attacks powered by AI mounts, Andrew Bailey said advances in quantum computing - which could unlock passwords - may add fresh dangers.
text:
Don't worry about AI... Quantum computing might well get you first, Bank Of England boss warns
The governor of the Bank of England on Thursday sounded the alarm about a new technology which could 'go beyond' the major risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI).
Even as the threat of cyber attacks powered by AI mounts, Andrew Bailey said advances in quantum computing – which could unlock passwords – may add fresh dangers.
And Mr Bailey admitted that the increasing risks were likely to see households storing more cash at home in case of emergencies.

text:
Agence France-Presse (AFP), one of the world’s three biggest news agencies, has been hit by a cyberattack that forced it to take its AFP Forum content platform offline.
AFP Forum is one of the main platforms the agency’s clients use to browse and download its photos, videos and other content. Most French media are AFP clients.
“AFP was hit by a cyberattack overnight, starting at 1:30 am (Paris time). The target was AFP Forum, one of the platforms our clients use to browse and download our content,” an internal email from AFP management said, according to the agency’s report.
“As soon as the intrusion was detected, our teams moved immediately to contain the intrusion and took AFP Forum offline as a precautionary measure. AFP Forum remains unavailable until further notice,” it added.

text:
Beloved grizzly bear named Emmett dies at ripe old age of 21 after being euthanized by devastated zoo staff
A beloved grizzly bear at a zoo in Colorado was euthanized earlier this week after a devastating battle with cancer.
Emmett, the 21-year-old grizzly from Cheyenne Mountain Zoo (CMZoo) in Colorado Springs, Colorado was euthanized last Monday after his aggressive cancer, which affected his energy levels and mobility, returned in mid-October.
Emmett was first diagnosed with cancer in early 2026, and received a surgery to remove a mass from his tail in February, the zoo reported.
The surgery was successful, and Emmett was back in good shape throughout the spring and summer.
Unfortunately a biopsy from October showed that the cancer had returned and Emmett started exhibiting lethargy, disinterest in training, and a lack of appetite which stirred concern in zookeepers and trainers alike.

text:
Australia in the firing line for brutal heat as El Niño threatens to turn up the temperature this summer
Millions of Australians could be bracing for an unusually hot, relentless summer, with El Niño forecast to bring higher than average temperatures.
The Bureau of Meteorology has released its forecast outlook for the next three months just days out from the start of summer.
It follows a warmer than usual spring, during which both daytime and overnight temperatures were above average across much of Australia.
Last month was the warmest October on record globally, surpassing the previous record set in 2023.
'There is an increased risk of heatwaves because unusually hot days and warm nights are likely,' the bureau states.

text:
SHF News
Allocations
In the second and third quarters of 2026, the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) undertook three critical allocations to address urgent humanitarian needs. In July 2026, the SHF allocated US$ 2 million to scale up response required to mitigate the risk of famine in rural areas of Buurhakaba, Bay Region. The allocation prioritized multisectoral lifesaving assistance to increase access to food, integrated health, nutrition, and protection (GBV) services; and improve access to water. The allocation was complemented by a $10 million CERF Rapid Response grant to sustain humanitarian assistance to mitigate the adverse effects of the prolonged drought conditions in additional areas. Lee's approval rating rises for 2nd straight week: poll
SEOUL, Nov. 27 (Yonhap) -- President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating rose for the second consecutive week to 41 percent, a poll showed Friday.
The survey, conducted by Gallup Korea from Tuesday through Thursday on 1,000 people aged 18 and older, showed that positive assessments of Lee's performance gained 1 percentage point from the previous week.
Those who disapproved of Lee's handling of state affairs also rose 1 percentage point to 50 percent.
Lee's approval rating has fluctuated between 39 and 41 percent for seven weeks since mid-October.
Among those who positively assessed Lee's performance, 29 percent cited diplomacy, up from 24 percent the previous week, followed by economic and livelihood issues at 10 percent, and communication at 5 percent.

text:

text:
Australia’s far-right is on track for its best election result ever this weekend, with polls showing more than a fifth of voters in Victoria state will back One Nation in an expected rout of the ruling Labor party.
Led by the firebrand Pauline Hanson, One Nation has moved steadily to the center stage this year after decades on the political fringe. It’s expected to get 23% of the primary vote in the state election on Saturday, according to a poll published this week. That would be its best-ever performance in the state and outpace its strong showing earlier this year in South Australia.
That outcome would be particularly stark for Victoria, which has Melbourne as its capital and is among the most culturally diverse areas of the country.

South Korea proposed to discuss financial stability amid the spread of artificial intelligence (AI) as next year's key agenda.
Meanwhile, this year's meeting was held in Kyoto, Japan, on Wednesday and Thursday to discuss ways to strengthen regional financial cooperation.

أوهم عملاءه بحيازته آثارًا.. ضبط عاطل بتهمة النصب والاحتيال في قنا
تمكنت الأجهزة الأمنية بقنا من ضبط عاطل بتهمة النصب والاحتيال على المواطنين من خلال ايهامهم بحوزته قطع أثرية للبيع وطلب منهم تحويل اموال وذلك خلال صفحة يديرها على الفيسبوك.
كان قطاع شرطة السياحة والأثار قد رصد قيام أحد الأشخاص بإدارة صفحة بمواقع التواصل الإجتماعى للترويج لتجارة الآثار والزعم بحيازته لها.
بالفحص أمكن تحديد وضبط القائم على إدارة الصفحة المشار إليها وهو أحد الأشخاص "له معلومات جنائية" - مقيم بدائرة قسم شرطة قنا، وضُبط بحوزته «هاتف محمول "بفحصه تبين احتواءه على دلائل تؤكد نشاطه الإجرامي.
وتبين عدم حيازته لأية قطع أثرية، وبمواجهته اعترف بإنشاء وإدارة الصفحة المشار إليها بمواقع التواصل الاجتماعي ونشره صور قطع أثرية تحصل عليها من شبكة الإنترنت بقصد النصب والاحتيال على المواطنين وإيهام راغبي شرائها بحيازته لها وطلبه منهم تحويل مبالغ مالية وغلق هاتفه عقب ذلك، فتم اتخاذ الإجراءات القانونية.

title: Mone Chiba brushes off hostile reception from fans after win in China
summary: The world silver medalist won the Cup of China in Shenzhen this month and reports and social media users said she was booed as she stood on the podium.
text:
Figure skater Mone Chiba said Thursday that fans’ behavior is “not something I can control” after she reportedly received a hostile reception in China, with the sport’s governing body calling for more respect.

text:
QUETTA: A district and sessions court has granted bail to senior journalist Shahid Maitla and ordered his release against surety bonds worth Rs3 million.
District and Sessions Judge Quetta Ghulam Qadir Shah Bukhari announced the decision on a post-arrest bail petition filed by the journalist.
A case was registered against Shahid Maitla following a complaint submitted by former caretaker prime minister Anwaarul Haq Kakar to the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency. The NCCIA subsequently arrested Mr Maitla in Islamabad and transferred him to Quetta. He was later sent to jail under court orders.
Following his arrest, Mr Maitla had filed a post-arrest bail application before Judicial Magistrate Syed Akhtar Shah. However, the magistrate rejected his bail plea.
Subsequently, Mr Maitla , through his counsel Rahib Buleedi, approached the sessions court, which has granted him post-arrest bail.

text:
World Health Organization (WHO) Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, today announced US$ 1 million in support for critical medical equipment in Haiti. Dr Tedros made the announcement during his visit to the country to reinforce WHO’s support for a health system under severe pressure from the ongoing humanitarian and security crisis.
The funding will provide equipment to the overwhelmed Hôpital Universitaire La Paix (HUP) in the capital, Port-au-Prince, including a computed tomography (CT) scanner and equipment for four operating rooms. HUP is the last major public referral hospital still operating in Port-au-Prince, a city where half (49.5%) of health facilities are non-functional and just 12% are partially operational. Across Haiti, a country of more than 11 million people, almost one quarter (24.5%) of health facilities are not functioning, and close to half (48.5%) are operating only partially.

title: Sovereign wealth funds are acting more like private equity giants — and inheriting their risks
summary: Sovereign wealth funds are increasingly originating deals, taking controlling stakes and building their own investment platforms.
text:
For decades, sovereign wealth funds were among private equity's most deep-pocketed backers, entrusting billions of dollars to buyout firms to invest on their behalf. Increasingly, they are doing the dealmaking themselves.
From originating transactions and taking controlling stakes in companies to building their own investment platforms, some of the world's largest state investors are adopting the playbook of traditional private equity giants, according to industry veterans.
"The imminent change is that the lines between LPs and GPs are becoming increasingly blurry. This could bring more fundamental changes in the long term," Diego Lopez of Global SWF told CNBC.
Limited partners, or LPs, typically commit capital to private equity funds, while general partners, or GPs, are responsible for sourcing deals and managing investments.

LONDON/GENEVA, 27 November 2026 – Nearly one girl every three seconds is married before the age of 18 despite world leaders committing more than 10 years ago to end child marriage by 2030, said Save the Children said on the first International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage[1] [2].
Save the Children said progress at ending child marriage has slowed to a crawl, leaving millions of girls at risk of being denied their childhoods, education, safety and future opportunities.
Global child marriage rates have fallen by just 3.4 percentage points since 2014, from 21.9% to 18.5%, and have barely shifted in the last two years [3]. At the current pace, the world is dangerously off track to meet its commitment to end child marriage in the next four years with hard-won gains at risk of reversal, said the child rights organisation.

title: Father, 49, died after getting trapped in fake cave at climbing centre for hours during child's birthday party: Cumbria business is fined £67,500
summary: Carl O'Keeffe, 49, suffered fatal crush injuries after he became trapped inside an artificial cave for five hours at King Kong Climbing Centre in Keswick, Cumbria, in April 2023.
text:
Father, 49, died after getting trapped in fake cave at climbing centre for hours during child's birthday party: Cumbria business is fined £67,500
A father suffered fatal crush injuries after he became trapped inside an artificial cave for five hours during a family birthday outing.
Carl O'Keeffe, a PhD graduate from Lancaster, was freed by specialist rescuers after becoming wedged inside a narrow, 65ft-long fibreglass tunnel at King Kong Climbing Centre in Keswick, Cumbria, in April 2023.
The 49-year-old, who was at the centre for a children's birthday, died in hospital eight days later on April 30 from multiple organ failure.
The climbing centre and its company director Paul Cornforth, 64, admitted a breach of the Health and Safety at Work Act.
On Thursday, the company was fined £67,500, with a £2,000 surcharge fee, and £20,000 costs contribution at Newcastle Crown Court.
Judge Edward Bindloss said the cave system was a 'very bad design' and there had been 'no emergency plan in place'

title: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney who turned $600 with his brother into global pizza empire dies aged 95
summary: Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney founded the restaurant with his brother Frank in 1958.
text:
Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney who turned $600 with his brother into global pizza empire dies aged 95
Pizza Hut co-founder Dan Carney who turned a $600 loan with his brother into a global fast-food empire has died at 95.
The pizza magnate's family said he passed away ‘peacefully’ on November 13, and his son Michael told the New York Times that his father died from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Carney founded Pizza Hut with his brother Frank - who passed away in 2020 - in 1958 after they borrowed a small loan of startup capital from their mother, Mary.
The brothers transformed the single location restuarant in Wichita, Kansas, into one of the most popular restaurant chains in the world.
The Carney brothers began franchising a year into their business in 1959, and expanded the business internationally in 1970.
After the brothers' company boomed, the duo sold the chain to PepsiCo for $300 million in 1977 - becoming one of the great business family success stories in the Midwest.

title: IAEA in talks with Russia, Ukraine on ceasefire around ZNPP — Grossi
summary: The official called on both sides to "work constructively" to facilitate repair of the Ferrosplavnaya-1 line and re-establish an offsite power connection to the plant
text:
VIENNA, November 27. /TASS/. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is negotiating with Russia and Ukraine about a cessation of hostilities around the Zaporozhye Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) following a yet another power outage, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said.
"Once again we are faced with a loss of offsite power at the ZNPP. Its continued reliance on a single power line, together with the plant’s location on the front line of an active warzone, results in an extremely precarious offsite power connection," he said.
"I call on both sides to work constructively with the IAEA to cease military activity against electrical infrastructure, facilitate repair of the Ferrosplavnaya-1 line and re-establish an offsite power connection to the ZNPP," the official added.
On Wednesday morning, the IAEA reported that the ZNPP had completely lost its external power supply for the 28th time since the start of the conflict in Ukraine and switched to emergency diesel generators.

"This latest escalation is a direct consequence of the lack of law enforcement and the sense of impunity enjoyed by the perpetrators," said Ghiath Nasser, a lawyer representing the owners of the houses in court.
The demolition follows a surge of settler violence in which settlers have encroached on Palestinian villages, with an average of 53 settler attacks per week since the start of 2026, according to UN figures.

title: 314 years after Dutch ship sank off Australia, 23 stolen silver coins return from California and Amsterdam
summary: After extensive efforts, Australia has reclaimed twenty-three silver coins from the infamous Zuytdorp shipwreck, which was lost at sea in 1712. The recovery operations spanned both the Netherlands and the United States, revealing a surge in illicit interest since 2019. In light of this, Australian authorities ramped up their monitoring, culminating in local resident Ashley Patterson's guilty plea for breaching underwater heritage laws linked to these invaluable artifacts.
text:
A shipwreck that lay beneath the waters off Western Australia for more than three centuries has become the centre of an international investigation, with 23 silver coins stolen from its seabed finally returning to Australia. The coins, taken from the Dutch East India Company vessel Zuytdorp, were recovered in the Netherlands and the United States and formally handed back to Australian authorities on November 24, 2026, according to a joint media release by the Australian government and a report by ABC News.
The Zuytdorp disappeared in 1712 while travelling from the Netherlands to Batavia, now Jakarta, carrying a valuable cargo that included 128,000 Dutch guilders worth of silver coins. The ship sank off the coast of Western Australia, between Kalbarri and Shark Bay, in circumstances that remain unknown. Around 200 people were aboard, but unlike the crews of some other Dutch vessels wrecked along the coast, the Zuytdorp's survivors were never heard from again.

BRUSSELS, Nov 26 - EU leaders will try to reach an agreement on the next long term budget for the EU this year, but will not reconvene for new talks on Friday, German chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday evening.
Merz said a day of talks between EU leaders in Brussels had brought "new movement" towards a reduction of the proposed size of the next budget, as demanded by Germany and other countries who are net contributors to the bloc's finances.
The leaders will try to hammer out a deal during a two-day summit starting December 17, Merz said.

text: For decades, scientists have attempted to develop power devices that can harvest the osmotic energy created by the natural difference in salinity where a freshwater river meets the salty sea, a source of clean, renewable energy also known as blue energy. Most osmotic power devices rely on reverse electrodialysis (RED), wherein freshwater and saltwater meet across charged membranes pierced with nanoscale channels. As salt ions move through these channels to balance concentrations, they generate an electric current. Prototypes have delivered a tiny fraction of the power lab models promise, according to Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU). Marie-Antoinette’s ‘nipple bowl’ auctioned for record US$3.1 million
PARIS - A rare porcelain cup in the shape of a woman’s breast which once belonged to French Queen Marie-Antoinette fetched a record €2.9 million (S$4.1 million) at auction on Nov 26.
Complete with a moulded pink-tinged ceramic nipple, the late 18th-century masterpiece from the renowned Sevres porcelain factory was thought lost for two centuries before its chance rediscovery in the inventory of the Meyer Gallery in Paris.
The “jatte-teton”, meaning nipple bowl, was one of four such pieces which King Louis XVI once ordered for Marie-Antoinette’s dairy creamery at the royal residence in Rambouillet, south-west of the capital.
The Austrian-born royal was notorious for her extravagant spending, contributing to the souring of public opinion against the monarchy ahead of her execution by guillotine in October 1793 at the age of 37.

text:
President Javier Milei’s overhauled charter for Argentina’s Central Bank won final congressional approval on Thursday, a symbolic victory for the libertarian economist who campaigned on abolishing the monetary authority.
The bill to reform the charter passed the lower house in a 141 to 0 vote, with 99 abstentions. It had secured initial approval in that chamber in August but didn’t get through the Senate until September, with modifications. Thursday’s vote fell short of the two-thirds majority Milei needed to restore his original wording, though the legislation still essentially bans the Central Bank from financing government spending in the future.
Senators had simplified the mechanism for removing Central Bank authorities, requiring 37 votes, or a majority, in the upper chamber instead of the two-thirds majority in both chambers that Milei originally proposed. The same threshold will suffice to appoint them.

title: US postpones publication of review of its military presence in Europe until 2027 — portal
summary: The review, initiated by Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth in June and aimed at reducing the US military presence, was scheduled to last six months
text:
BRUSSELS, November 26. /TASS/. The United States has postponed the announcement of the results of its review of the US military presence in Europe, initially scheduled for December, until next year, the Brussels-based Rapporteur portal reported, citing diplomatic sources.
The review process, initiated by Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth in June, was scheduled to last six months, with its findings due to be presented in December. Its goal is to reduce the US military presence in Europe and cut the amount of resources Washington could provide to its NATO allies in the event of a crisis.
This comes as US President Donald Trump’s administration urges its allies to assume greater responsibility for the conventional forces needed to defend the continent. At the same time, Washington is seeking to redirect resources to other regions, primarily the Asia-Pacific.
